diagnostics.message: :resource.aws_autoscaling_group.ng: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_iam_role.ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.ng: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_launch_template.ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.aws_eks_node_group.ng: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_iam_role.ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references

aws_autoscaling_group.ng explicitly depends_on aws_launch_template.ng, but it already references the same launch template in its mixed_instances_policy block, so Terraform already infers this ordering.
aws_autoscaling_group.ng explicitly depends_on aws_iam_role.ng, but it already depends on that role transitively through aws_launch_template.ng -> aws_iam_instance_profile.ng -> aws_iam_role.ng.
aws_eks_node_group.ng explicitly depends_on aws_iam_role.ng, but node_role_arn already references that role, so the explicit depends_on duplicates an implicit dependency.

kubernetes_config_map.aws-auth explicitly depends_on aws_eks_cluster.cp, but it already depends on the cluster transitively through aws_autoscaling_group.ng (and through the Kubernetes provider configuration).

When App Mesh is enabled, aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.xray-write attaches the X-Ray write policy to the node role, but aws_autoscaling_group.ng does not depend on that attachment. Instances can launch before the policy is attached.

When App Mesh is enabled, aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.xray-write attaches the X-Ray write policy to the managed node group's role, but aws_eks_node_group.ng does not depend on that attachment. Nodes can be created before the policy is attached.
